sections.text: Maria Short opened a “Popular Observatory” in Edinburgh in 1835 and later moved her observatory to the Royal Mile. The Camera Obscura uses optics to project a live image of the city, making observation itself the attraction.

sections.heading: From observatory to public learning
sections.text: Patrick Geddes later called the building the Outlook Tower and developed it as a centre for learning about the city. The site connects science, urban study and public curiosity.

sections.heading: A university city
sections.text: Cambridge’s collegiate structure has shaped architecture, scholarship and public life over centuries. Its colleges grew at different times, so the city is a collection of distinct institutional and architectural histories.

sections.heading: Learning in the landscape
sections.text: The archive names the university generally, not an individual college or academic activity. The story stays with the connection between place, learning and the built environment.

sections.heading: Canals as urban design
sections.text: Amsterdam’s historic canal district grew during the Dutch Golden Age as a planned expansion around concentric waterways. The canals served transport, trade, water management and urban form; houses and bridges express that relationship between city and water.

sections.heading: A later museum encounter
sections.text: The 2024 location record names Moco Museum, housed in Villa Alsberg on Museumplein. Its collection focuses on modern and contemporary art. The archive confirms a place tag and media count, but not which works or exhibition appear.

firstPerson: I have separate archive records for Ulm Minster and Fort Oberer Kuhberg across 2016 and 2017. They remain two moments in the chronology.

sections.heading: The Minster and a civic skyline
sections.text: Ulm Minster’s long construction history and prominent tower make it a landmark of medieval civic ambition. Its scale and position place sacred architecture at the centre of Ulm’s urban identity.

sections.heading: A fort with a difficult later history
sections.text: Fort Oberer Kuhberg formed part of Ulm’s nineteenth-century federal fortress. In 1933–35, part of it was used as an early Nazi concentration camp; this history is essential to interpreting the site. The 2017 location record does not state what rooms or interpretation I saw.

sections.heading: A city shaped by many administrations
sections.text: Timișoara’s history reflects Habsburg-era urban planning, Central European exchange and modern Romanian history. Its built environment includes layered civic architecture; the 1989 revolution began in the city before spreading across the country.
